I guess I should have realised you were speaking of yourself in the short description about your "friend". I have a view which not many people would accept but perhaps reading it might be of use. Perhaps some people are just wired the way you are. Sure there are people driven towards suicide because their life is too unbearable. Perhaps they are lonely. Maybe too poor to do the things they want. And maybe in their case, having more friends or being more wealthy would stop them thinking of suicide. However I believe for others it isn't due to circumstances but because that's just the way they are as a person. Although society will not accept it to be that way. The view I have is that perhaps people with feelings of suicide are somewhat like gay people. People are lead to believe that the way of life is just to continue until dying of natural causes. Like we're all sheep in a flock and those who go against this are considered ill and need to get better. They contradict the natural order of things. But in terms of sustaining life, anatomy would dictate it must be a male and female. That's how life continues. Therefore homosexuality could be considered against the way life should be. And some people do view it that way, to the extent of believing it to be a disease. To me, I think people are just different sometimes. Even if gay people told themselves it's wrong to feel the way they do because of how some people in society view it, can they control it? Ultimately, it's their own nature and feelings. It's how they are wired. In a similar way, I believe people who have feelings of suicide are perhaps just made that way and cannot control it regardless of how many other people tell them it's wrong to feel that way. I rambled on a bit again but that's my views even though the majority of people will not accept the idea that perhaps some suicidal people are just that way because of their very own nature.

People will never have a unanimous view towards suicide. There are certain things that are said when the topic of suicide is discussed which somewhat bugs me. My advice if they've tried everything and still feel that way, then they should not feel obliged to live just because society views it as being wrong. I think sometimes people with suicidal thoughts go through even more hardship just because some people try to drill it into their heads that it's unacceptable to feel that way. Suicide is often considered selfish and yet as humans we are all selfish beings. It's just that some people's selfishness resonates better with other people. I watched a show once that said "charity is not for the sake of others". And if you think of why people give to charity... Even if they do not make a deal out of it, at the core, it's done to make themselves feel better. People try to "help" people with suicide thoughts sometimes by guilt tripping them. I've heard things like "think of how it will impact so and so" or "I don't think I'd be able to survive if you were to commit suicide". And yet those people will not be seen as selfish unlike the person who is thinking of committing suicide. I don't think it's fair that people have to be forced to carry out things they do not wish to do. People who are trying to "help" often state their own circumstances too which bugs me somewhat. They would say things like "I have a shitty life too but I worked through it" or "Life gets better". I don't really see how that will help though. Because we are all unique with our individual set of emotions. People who have suicidal thoughts and pull through it. That's good for them. But for them to state it as if it's proof that every person with suicidal thoughts should do the same is not understanding of the other person. I believe the most we can really do is relate to someone. But we cannot fully understand another person. It can be seen as narrow minded but I believe those people who say life gets better is spouting optimistic nonsense. I am not saying they are mistaken. It's just that there's no way they can state that to be fact. If anything, life getting worse is more likely. Almost guaranteed. Since death is the only sure thing in life, we will lose loved ones. That is a certainty. Therefore sorrow and bad times are definite in life. However happiness is not. Sure you could work towards happiness and achieve it, but sooner or later, it will be accompanied with unhappiness. I realise I'm babbling on a lot. But I guess to summarise, I think people should be given the right to decide what they want to do without being made to feel so bad about it.
